slides.title: Scheduling Queues & Schedulers
content: Scheduling organizes processes into queues such as job queue (all processes), ready queue (waiting for CPU), and device queue (waiting for I/O)
Processes move between queues during execution based on events like I/O requests, interrupts, or completion
Long-term scheduler selects processes from job queue and controls degree of multiprogramming
Short-term scheduler selects processes from ready queue for CPU execution frequently
Medium-term scheduler swaps processes in and out of memory to manage system load

slides.title: Process Scheduling Basics
content: Process scheduling determines the order in which processes execute to maximize CPU utilization and system performance
It considers factors like arrival time, burst time, priority, and I/O or CPU-bound nature of processes
It ensures fairness, prevents starvation, and meets deadlines in real-time systems
Scheduling improves throughput, response time, and overall system efficiency

slides.title: Preemptive vs Non-Preemptive
content: Preemptive scheduling allows the OS to interrupt a running process and assign CPU to another process
It provides high responsiveness and is used in real-time and interactive systems but adds context switching overhead
Non-preemptive scheduling allows a process to run until completion without interruption
It is simple and has low overhead but may lead to poor responsiveness and starvation

slides.title: FCFS, SJF, SRTF
content: FCFS (First Come First Serve) executes processes in arrival order and is simple but suffers from convoy effect
SJF (Shortest Job First) selects the process with the shortest burst time and minimizes average waiting time
SRTF (Shortest Remaining Time First) is a preemptive version of SJF that always executes the shortest remaining job
SJF and SRTF improve efficiency but may cause starvation of longer processes

slides.title: HRRN, Round Robin, Priority
content: HRRN (Highest Response Ratio Next) selects processes based on response ratio to balance waiting time and execution time
Round Robin scheduling assigns CPU for a fixed time slice to each process ensuring fairness
Priority scheduling executes processes based on priority levels and can be preemptive or non-preemptive
Round Robin improves responsiveness while priority scheduling handles critical tasks efficiently

slides.title: MLQ & MLFQ Scheduling
content: Multilevel Queue (MLQ) divides processes into different queues based on type with separate scheduling policies
Each queue may use algorithms like FCFS, Round Robin, or priority scheduling
Multilevel Feedback Queue (MLFQ) allows processes to move between queues based on behavior and execution history
MLFQ is adaptive, reduces starvation, and balances performance but is complex to implement
